body:
Sarvam Maya delivers a soothing, feel-good supernatural dramedy that leans on familiar emotional beats but holds the audience effortlessly for its runtime.

Nivin Pauly shines in his signature style, with expressions and mannerisms that audiences adore, carrying the role with the same easy charm as in his best works. Riya Shibu emerges as the real standout, outshining others on screen with a bubbly, memorable ghost persona that fits her perfectly and sparks curiosity about her future range.

Supporting players like Aju Varghese, Janardhanan, and Raghunath Paleri slot in seamlessly, while Preity Mukhundan adds quiet beauty to her brief part.

Director Akhil Sathyan recycles seen-before scenarios laced with ghostly whimsy, blending laughs, tears, and warmth in a rollercoaster that feels comforting rather than groundbreaking-earning it a spot above his debut Pachuvum Athbhuthavilakkum for many.

Overall, it caps 2025 on a happy, undemanding high, perfect for a light watch that tugs at the heartstrings without overreaching.

One of the few movies that made me genuinely laugh in the past few years. Everyone from children to elders can watch this movie and get entertained. The comedy is good also it shows some social commentary on today's generation. Also actor nivin pauly brought his natural charisma back into the big screen after a long time and entertained us like this.

"Sarvam Maya" is a feel-good ghost movie, and hats off to the director for effectively using the female characters. The ways in which women-such as mothers, spouses, friends, and sisters-shape a man's life are well portrayed. For instance, the main character's mother has a significant impact, and the ghost who becomes a friend is also well executed. One standout feature of this movie, which is lacking in many recent films, is the commendable ending that provides closure for all the characters. Additionally, the film humorously incorporates various myths while telling its ghost story, which is fantastic. Overall, it's a light-hearted movie that leaves you feeling stress-free.

Sarvam Maya isn't your typical ghost story-it's a quiet, layered film that gently blurs the line between reality and illusion, just as its title suggests.

From the very beginning, the film sets a soft, almost dreamy tone. The story of Prabhendu unfolds not with loud horror or jump scares, but with a sense of lingering emptiness and curiosity. Nivin Pauly delivers one of his most restrained and mature performances, portraying a man caught between duty, doubt, and an unexplainable connection with something-or someone-beyond logic.

The character of Maya becomes the heart of the film. She is playful, mysterious, and deeply melancholic at the same time. Their relationship never feels forced; instead, it grows naturally, making you question whether she truly exists or is just a reflection of Prabhendu's inner loneliness.

What stands out most is the film's refusal to follow conventional horror tropes. There are no exaggerated scares-only a constant, subtle unease.

The music and visuals complement this mood beautifully, creating an atmosphere that feels both comforting and haunting. However, the film isn't without flaws. The pacing in the second half slightly dips, and the climax, while meaningful, might feel understated or even ambiguous to viewers expecting a clear resolution.

Yet, that ambiguity is also its strength. Sarvam Maya doesn't aim to give answers-it leaves you with questions.

In the end, it feels less like a horror film and more like a meditative experience about loneliness and the stories our minds create to survive it.

I am not Indian; I am Sri lanka. By the end of this film, I found myself questioning why I even watched it... I have always been a huge fan of Malayalam cinema, and once again, it proved that Malayalam movies are nothing short of magic. Everything-the music, the emotions, the advice, the story, and the plot-was executed perfectly. This is truly a masterpiece. It was so powerful that it managed to melt even my heart, which I thought was as hard as a stone.
